service.name: Gala and award night entertainment
service.serviceType: Live music for galas, fundraisers, award dinners and annual meetings
service.description: Live music for nonprofit galas, association award nights, chamber annual dinners and company award ceremonies in Denver and across Colorado: reception acts, dinner ensembles and dance bands that work around remarks, auctions, videos and walk-ups, on one contract.

faqs.q: How does the band handle award walk-ups?
faqs.a: Each honoree gets a short piece of music from the moment their name is read to the moment they reach the podium, cut on arrival rather than faded out over the first line of their speech. We take the list of names and the order ahead of the night, agree the cue with your emcee, and the band watches the emcee on the night.

faqs.q: Do you play during the live auction and the paddle raise?
faqs.a: Only if the auctioneer wants a bed under the bidding, and most don't. The usual plan is silence through the auction, a short piece as each lot closes if the program calls for it, and the band back in when the auctioneer hands the microphone back. The auctioneer gets a microphone of their own.

faqs.q: Can one booking cover the reception, dinner and the dance floor?
faqs.a: Yes, and it's the usual gala booking. A duo or a solo pianist as the doors open, the same musicians or a trio through dinner at 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table, and a dance band or the DJ after the last award, on one contract, one load-in and one sound system. The reception act and the dance floor act can be the same musicians or different ones; the contract doesn't change.

faqs.q: What do you need from the venue?
faqs.a: A dock time and an elevator window if it's a hotel, one or two dedicated 20-amp circuits depending on the size of the act, the venue's decibel cap and curfew if it has them, and the run of show with the program's cues on it. Footprints and power by size are published on our technical page so your venue contact can read them without a phone call.

faqs.q: Do you work with our emcee and auctioneer?
faqs.a: Yes. The run of show is planned with whoever is running the program, the emcee gets an announcement microphone of their own, and the bandleader takes cues from the emcee on the night. If your emcee is a board member doing it for the first time, we're happy to walk through it with them before the doors open.

faqs.q: How far ahead do galas book entertainment?
faqs.a: Committees usually work a year out from the date, because the venue and the honorees are settled first and the entertainment follows. The music is one vendor line that can be settled early. Tell us the date and the venue, and we'll come back with a recommendation and a price.
